title: Safe Sleep and Baby Bedding: What Belongs in the Cot
meta_description: What is safe in a baby's cot and what is not, for Pakistani homes. Bumpers, pillows, quilts, room temperature and how to use a bedding set safely.
keywords: baby safe sleep Pakistan, cot bedding safety, baby bedding set Pakistan, SIDS prevention, newborn sleep safety, nursery bedding guide
excerpt: A beautiful cot set and a safe cot are not automatically the same thing. Here is what belongs in the cot for sleep, and what is better used elsewhere.
imagePrompt: A neatly made baby cot in a bright nursery with a plain fitted cotton sheet on the mattress and nothing else inside. A folded muslin swaddle and a coordinated quilt rest on a wooden chair beside the cot, out of the cot. Soft morning light through a sheer curtain, warm neutral tones of cream and pale sage, calm editorial interior photography, no people, no text.

content.content:
Every new parent in Pakistan is shown the same photograph: a cot dressed with a padded bumper, a quilt folded at the foot, a small pillow, and two soft toys arranged in the corner. It is what a nursery is supposed to look like.

It is also not how a baby should sleep.

This is not an argument against buying a bedding set — a good one is genuinely useful and most of it has a place. It is about which parts go in the cot while the baby is sleeping and which parts belong on a chair, a shelf, or the floor until she is older. The distinction is worth getting right, and almost nobody explains it at the point of sale.

content.heading: The Rule, Stated Plainly
content.content:
For a baby under twelve months, the cot during sleep should contain: a firm flat mattress, a fitted sheet, and the baby.

That is the whole list.

No pillow, no quilt, no loose blanket, no cot bumper, no positioner or wedge, no toys. Loose bedding in a cot is a suffocation risk, and it is the single clearest thing safe-sleep guidance agrees on internationally.

This feels stark, and it looks bare compared with the photographs. But an empty cot is what safe looks like, and everything else in the set has a use — just not inside the cot while she is asleep.

content.heading: What About Cot Bumpers?
content.content:
Bumpers are the most common item in Pakistani cot sets and the one most worth reconsidering.

The original argument for them was preventing a baby's limbs slipping through the bars, or bumping her head. In practice, a padded bumper creates a soft surface a baby can turn her face into, and once she can pull up she can use it as a step to climb out.

Modern guidance is consistently against padded bumpers for sleep. If your cot has widely spaced bars and you are worried about limbs, a firm mesh liner is the alternative — it is breathable and does not create a soft surface.

Padded bumpers are not useless. They are perfectly fine on a daybed or a floor play area for an older child, and many families keep them for the toddler bed later. They just should not be in the cot for infant sleep.

content.heading: Keeping a Baby Warm Without Loose Bedding
content.content:
This is the practical question underneath everything, especially for a Lahore or Islamabad winter.

**Sleep sacks and wearable blankets** are the answer. The baby wears the warmth rather than lying under it, so nothing can ride up over her face. They come in different weights for different seasons.

**Layer clothing rather than adding blankets.** A vest under a sleepsuit is warmer and safer than a blanket over the top.

**Swaddling** works for young babies, using a thin muslin, wrapped firmly around the body but loose at the hips. Stop swaddling as soon as she shows any sign of rolling.

**Judge temperature at the chest, not the hands.** Babies have cool hands and feet even when perfectly warm. Slide a hand onto her chest or the back of her neck — warm and dry is correct. Sweaty means too hot, which is its own risk.

The room should sit around 16–20°C. In a Karachi summer that usually means a fan or air conditioning and a single thin layer; in a Murree winter it means a warmer sleep sack rather than more blankets.

content.heading: So What Is the Bedding Set For?
content.content:
A good set is not wasted. Most of it simply has a different timeline.

**Fitted sheets** — used from day one, and you want several. This is the part you will replace most often and the part worth buying extra of.

**Quilt or duvet** — for the floor as a play mat, for the pram, for a lap cover while feeding, and in the cot once she is over about a year old.

**Bumper** — for the toddler bed or daybed later, or a floor play area.

**Pillow** — from around two years, once she is in a bed rather than a cot.

**Muslins and swaddles** — the most used item in the set. Burp cloth, sun shade, feeding cover, swaddle, floor blanket.

content.heading: The Mattress Matters More Than the Set
content.content:
Parents research bedding carefully and often give the mattress no thought at all. It is the more important purchase.

**Firm, not soft.** Press your hand into it — it should not hold an impression. A soft mattress conforms around the face, which is exactly what you are trying to avoid.

**Correctly sized.** There should be no gap between the mattress edge and the cot frame. If you can fit two fingers down the side, the gap is too big and a limb or head can become wedged.

**Flat.** Not tilted, not wedged, no incline. Sleep positioners and incline wedges are marketed heavily and are not recommended.

**Waterproof protector under the sheet.** Not a plastic sheet loose on top. A fitted protector under the fitted sheet keeps the mattress usable and stays put.

content.heading: Fabric and Skin: What to Look For
content.content:
Newborn skin is thinner and more reactive than adult skin, and this is where quality genuinely shows.

**Pure cotton against the skin.** Breathable, absorbent, and washes at high temperature. Polyester blends trap heat and are the most common cause of a hot, restless baby.

**Check the dye.** Ask whether dyes are baby-safe and free of azo compounds. Wash everything before first use regardless — this removes residual finishing chemicals as well as loose dye.

**Avoid decorative trims inside the cot.** Ribbons, lace edging and appliqué on a fitted sheet all create loose material and small parts. Keep the sheet plain and put the decoration on the things outside the cot.

**Wash at 60°C.** Baby bedding needs a hotter wash than adult bedding, so check the care label before buying — a set that can only be washed cool is impractical.

content.heading: A Simple Setup That Is Both Safe and Looks Right
content.content:
You do not have to choose between a safe cot and a nursery you are happy with.

Inside the cot: firm mattress, waterproof protector, fitted sheet in a plain colour. Nothing else.

Around the cot: this is where the coordinated set does its work. The quilt folded over the end rail or on a nearby chair, cushions on the feeding chair, a wall hanging, a mobile fixed well out of reach.

The photograph still looks beautiful — arguably better, because an empty cot with a well-dressed room reads as calm rather than cluttered.

Then move things in as she grows: pillow at two, quilt in the cot at one, bumper never for infant sleep.

questions.question: Are cot bumpers safe for newborns?
questions.answer: No. Padded bumpers create a soft surface a baby can turn her face into, and once she can pull up she can use one to climb out. If you are worried about limbs slipping between bars, use a firm breathable mesh liner instead. Keep the padded bumper for a toddler bed or floor play area later.

questions.question: How do I keep my baby warm in winter without a blanket?
questions.answer: Use a sleep sack or wearable blanket in a weight suited to the season, and layer clothing underneath rather than adding covers on top. Check her temperature at the chest or the back of the neck, not the hands — babies have cool hands even when perfectly warm.

questions.question: When can my baby have a pillow and quilt in the cot?
questions.answer: A quilt from around twelve months, and a pillow from around two years once she has moved to a bed. Before that both are suffocation risks. Until then, the quilt is genuinely useful as a play mat, a pram cover or a lap blanket while feeding.

questions.question: What should I look for in a baby mattress?
questions.answer: Firm enough that it does not hold a handprint, sized so there is no gap at the cot edge, and completely flat with no incline. Add a fitted waterproof protector underneath the sheet rather than a loose plastic sheet on top.

questions.question: Should I wash new baby bedding before using it?
questions.answer: Yes, always, and at 60°C. A first wash removes residual finishing chemicals from manufacturing as well as any loose dye. Check the care label before buying too — baby bedding needs a hot wash regularly, so a set that can only be washed cool is impractical.
